concepts.name: Embedding Fragments in Compose with AndroidFragment
Resuming downloads with Range and If-Range

questions.prompt: During a Views-to-Compose migration, a new Compose screen must show a legacy `ReceiptFragment`. What is the recommended way to embed it?

choices.text: `AndroidViewBinding` around a layout with a `FragmentContainerView`
`AndroidView { ReceiptFragment().requireView() }` in its factory
A `ComposeView` that hosts the Fragment inside its `setContent`
`AndroidFragment<ReceiptFragment>()`, from `fragment-compose`

questions.explanation: `AndroidFragment` from `androidx.fragment:fragment-compose` adds the Fragment to the composition, removes it when it leaves the composition, and saves and restores its state. `AndroidViewBinding` with a `FragmentContainerView` is the older approach and no longer recommended. Either way it's a migration step: a Compose-only app shouldn't use Fragments.

sources.title: Using Views in Compose
sources.claim: The `AndroidFragment` composable (androidx.fragment:fragment-compose) adds a Fragment to the composition, removes it when the composable leaves the composition and saves its state; the AndroidViewBinding plus FragmentContainerView approach is no longer recommended; use AndroidFragment only during incremental migration.

questions.prompt: Your downloader resumes a half-done file with `Range: bytes=5000000-` and `If-Range: "v7"`, the ETag it saw before. The server answers `200 OK`. What should the client do?

choices.text: Append the body to the partial file, starting at byte 5,000,000
Retry without `If-Range`, so the server must return a 206 instead
Discard the partial file and save this body as the entire file
Fail the download, as a range request must get a 206 or a 416

questions.explanation: A `200` to a range request means the server is sending the entire representation: either the `If-Range` validator no longer matches (the file changed) or the server ignored `Range`, which it may do. Appending would corrupt the file, and dropping `If-Range` risks stitching bytes of two different versions together.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.claim: A server MAY ignore the Range header field; If-Range means "if the representation is unchanged, send me the parts in Range; otherwise send me the entire representation", and a recipient MUST ignore Range when the If-Range condition is false; 206 indicates parts of the representation are being transferred.

questions.prompt: A video app shows a player with a list of related videos. Which canonical adaptive layout fits, how does it behave from compact to expanded widths, and why not list-detail?

model_answer.summary: The supporting pane layout: the player is the main content and related videos a supporting pane beside it on wide windows, moved below it or into a sheet on compact widths; list-detail is for picking an item from a list to see its detail.
key_points: Supporting pane splits the window into primary content, taking most of the space, and a secondary pane that supports it, such as related videos
On expanded widths the two panes sit side by side; on compact widths the supporting content goes below the main content or into a bottom or side sheet
List-detail is for browsing a list and showing the selected item's detail, one pane at a time on smaller widths, which doesn't match a player with suggestions
In Compose it is built with `SupportingPaneScaffold` from Material 3 adaptive, driven by a navigator's scaffold directive and value

questions.explanation: The three canonical layouts answer different needs: list-detail for selecting items, supporting pane for main content with helpers, feed for a grid of equal items. Picking list-detail because the screen has a list is the tempting mistake.

sources.title: Canonical layouts
sources.claim: The supporting pane layout organises content into a primary area and a secondary pane that supports it (e.g. a video with related videos); on expanded widths they are side by side, on compact widths the supporting content goes below the main content or in a bottom or side sheet; it's built with SupportingPaneScaffold. List-detail shows a list and a selected item's detail, one at a time on smaller widths.

questions.prompt: A `HorizontalPager` shows one `AndroidFragment` per page. With Fragment 1.9.0+, how do you keep pages other than the settled one from being resumed?

choices.text: Call `onPause()` on those Fragments from a `LaunchedEffect`
Pass `maxLifecycle`: RESUMED only on the settled page, else STARTED
Use the `onUpdate` callback to detach them as the pages scroll
Wrap each page in `key(page)`, so its Fragment restarts on every swipe

questions.explanation: Since Fragment 1.9.0, `AndroidFragment` takes a `maxLifecycle` that caps the Fragment's lifecycle state, and the docs show exactly this pager pattern: `RESUMED` for `pagerState.settledPage` and `STARTED` otherwise. Calling lifecycle methods yourself bypasses the `FragmentManager`.

sources.title: Using Views in Compose
sources.claim: In Fragment 1.9.0+, AndroidFragment's `maxLifecycle` parameter caps the lifecycle state, which is useful in lazy layouts like HorizontalPager: RESUMED for the settled page and STARTED otherwise.

questions.prompt: Design resume support for large file downloads in your app's downloader. What does the client store and send, and how does it handle each response?

model_answer.summary: Store the bytes written and the file's strong ETag, resume with `Range` plus `If-Range`, append on 206 and start over on 200, since the server may have ignored the range or the file changed.
key_points: Persist how many bytes are on disk and a strong validator for the file, preferably its ETag (a weak ETag must not be used in `If-Range`)
Resume with `Range: bytes=<offset>-` and `If-Range: <etag>`, so the server sends only the rest if the file is unchanged
On `206 Partial Content`, append the body at the offset given by `Content-Range`
On `200 OK`, the server sent the whole file, because it changed or the server ignored `Range`: replace the partial file instead of appending

questions.explanation: `If-Range` turns two round trips into one: "the rest if unchanged, else everything". A downloader that sends only `Range` and appends blindly can join the start of one version to the end of another.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.claim: A server MAY ignore Range; If-Range sends the requested parts if the representation is unchanged and the entire representation otherwise; a client MUST NOT send a weak entity tag in If-Range; 206 Partial Content transfers one or more parts of the selected representation.

questions.prompt: Which screen best fits the supporting pane canonical layout, rather than list-detail or feed?

choices.text: An inbox where picking a message shows its whole text beside it
A news app with a grid of equally weighted article cards on it
A document editor with a pane of reviewer comments next to it
A contacts app where tapping a name opens that person's profile

questions.explanation: Supporting pane is for main content plus secondary content that supports it, such as a document with reviewer comments. An inbox or contacts app is list-detail (pick an item, see its detail), and a grid of equivalent cards is the feed layout.

sources.title: Canonical layouts
sources.claim: List-detail suits messaging and contact managers; supporting pane suits a document with reviewer comments or a video with related videos; feed arranges equivalent content in a grid.

questions.prompt: A video app shows a player with a list of related videos. Which statements match Android's canonical layouts guide? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Supporting pane fits: the related videos support the main video
List-detail fits better, since the related videos form a list of items
On compact widths the related videos go below the player or in a bottom sheet
On compact widths the related videos are hidden, since they can't fit at all
In Compose it is built with `SupportingPaneScaffold` from Material 3 adaptive

questions.explanation: The guide gives a streaming video with a list of related videos as a supporting pane use case: the primary content takes most of the window and the secondary pane supports it, meaningful only next to it. List-detail is for detail that stands on its own, like a product description. On compact widths the supporting content goes below the main content or into a bottom sheet rather than disappearing, and in Compose the layout is `SupportingPaneScaffold`.

sources.title: Canonical layouts
sources.claim: Supporting pane splits the window into primary content and a secondary pane that is meaningful only in relation to it (e.g. a streaming video and related videos); on compact widths the supporting content goes below the main content or in a bottom sheet; it is built with SupportingPaneScaffold. List-detail detail content is meaningful on its own.

questions.prompt: Your downloader resumes a large file with `Range: bytes=<offset>-` and `If-Range: <etag>`. Which statements hold under RFC 9110? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A `206 Partial Content` reply has a `Content-Range` saying which bytes it holds
A `200 OK` reply is the whole file, so replace the partial file, don't append
A weak ETag such as `W/"v1"` is fine in `If-Range` if the file rarely changes
A server must honour `Range`, so a `200 OK` reply means the request was malformed
If the ETag no longer matches, the server ignores `Range` and sends the whole file

questions.explanation: With `If-Range`, the server processes `Range` only if the validator still matches; otherwise it ignores `Range` and sends the whole representation. A server MAY also ignore `Range` anyway, so a `200 OK` is a full file to replace the partial one with, not an error. A `206 Partial Content` reply says in `Content-Range` which bytes it carries. A client MUST NOT send a weak entity tag in `If-Range`.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.claim: A server MAY ignore Range; with If-Range the server processes Range only if the validator matches and otherwise ignores it and sends the entire representation; a client MUST NOT generate If-Range with a weak entity tag; a 206 response carries Content-Range.
